evidence.quote: we report the CO abundance relative to H$_{2}$ derived toward the circumstellar disk of the T-Tauri star TW Hya from the HD ($1-0$) and C$^{18}$O ($2-1$) emission lines.

method.value: Compare 13CO and C18O flux ratio with assumed isotope ratios

evidence.quote: we compare C$^{18}$O ($2-1$) to $^{13}$CO ($2-1$) and find the disk-averaged $^{13}$CO/C$^{18}$O flux ratio is $\sim$3.3 $\pm$ 0.9.
assuming isotope ratios of $\rm{^{12}C/^{13}C=70}$ and $\rm{^{16}O/^{18}O=557}$ for the local ISM

analysis_steps.goal: Derive chi(CO) from LTE flux ratio

method.value: Ratio of upper-state populations of C18O and HD, with chi(HD)=3e-5, varying HD temperature 20-60 K and C18O at 20 K

evidence.loc: Mass and Model Independent chi(CO) Determination
evidence.quote: we compute the $\chi$(CO) from Eq. [\[eq:abu\]](#eq:abu) assuming a C$^{18}$O gas temperature of $T_g=20$ K and varying the HD emitting temperature

evidence.quote: assuming the emission is co-spatial and in LTE

findings_qualitative.value: CO is likely an unreliable H2 mass tracer

evidence.quote: CO may be an unreliable tracer of H$_2$ gas mass.

claims.hypothesis: TW Hya warm layer has the canonical CO abundance of 1e-4
claims.experiment: Compare C18O (2-1) and HD (1-0) fluxes under LTE
claims.finding: CO is depleted by at least an order of magnitude, perhaps via chemical carbon sink

evidence.quote: substantially lower than the canonical value of $\chi{\rm(CO)}=10^{-4}$

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Freeze-out, photodissociation and different emitting regions considered and judged unlikely to explain low chi(CO)

evidence.quote: the reduced measured $\chi$(CO) in the gas-phase is unlikely to be the result of freeze-out

limitations_admitted.value: HD may be optically thick, so chi(CO) would be an upper limit

evidence.quote: the possibility of optically thick HD emission still remains

referee_caveats_inferred: Disk-averaged LTE analysis with large temperature uncertainty
Results depend on the HD abundance and the Gorti model
